chapters.title: The People of the House and the Prophet's Witness
Intellect, Not Reason
comprehension_flags: The text opposes tawil (glossed in the prose as a return to the "First") with tanzil, but leaves tanzil unexplained, so a modern reader may not grasp that it means the literal "sending down" of the revelation.

A general reader may stumble on the unglossed specialist terms carried over from the source — apophasis, antinomies, existentiation, supra-rational, ontologically — which this pass is not authorized to explain inline.
terminology_notes: The word for intellect appears in the source with varying transliteration ('aql, aql; al-aqil, 'aqil) — recommend standardizing one spelling of each book-wide.

chapters.title: The Discourse to Kumayl
terminology_notes: The transliterations of the terms for the knower and the intellect appear in the source both with and without the initial ayn ("'alim"/"alim", "'aqil"/"aqil"); the source spellings were preserved at each occurrence, but the ayn should be standardized book-wide.

chapters.title: The Fruits of Certainty
comprehension_flags: The author's hyphenated coinage "in-spiration of God's spirit" deliberately evokes a breathing-in of spirit, which a reader may not parse on first sight; it has been preserved as written rather than glossed.
terminology_notes: "epistemology of joy" — the source's coined phrase is rendered as "a way of knowing steeped in joy"; standardize whichever form the book adopts wherever the concept recurs.

chapters.title: A Sacred Conception of Justice
comprehension_flags: A general reader may stumble on the unglossed specialist vocabulary the argument leans on ("ontological principle," "radical incommensurability," "modes within being," "existential orientation," "the pure positivity of the Absolute"), which this pass is not authorized to explain.
terminology_notes: The divine name al-Haqq is rendered inconsistently across the source — sometimes script only (الحق, حق), sometimes transliteration beside script (al-Haqq, الحق / haqq, حق) — and should be standardized book-wide.

chapters.title: Conscience, Compassion, and the Ordering of Society
terminology_notes: al-nafs al-ammara / nafs al-ammara — the source uses both the full ("al-nafs al-ammara") and short ("nafs al-ammara") forms for the commanding soul; a book-wide pass should settle on one spelling.
the transliteration of سوء الظن — rendered 'su al-zann' in one place and 'su' zannihim' in another (against 'husn al-zann') — should be standardized book-wide.

chapters.title: Justice for the Poor and the Sincerity of Intention
editorial_queries: The sentence beginning "If one speaks the truth without grasping the reason for it..." runs its conditional clause into two embedded "that" clauses, so it is not fully clear whether those clauses state the reason one fails to grasp or are freestanding assertions; it has been read as the reason (that truth is the Creator's nature, and that the aim is to take on His qualities).
terminology_notes: "taste" — used in scare quotes for the inward experiential grasp of grace; should be rendered the same way at every occurrence book-wide.

chapters.title: Prayer, Remembrance, and Gazing on the Good
Dhikr: The Polish of the Heart
editorial_queries: The source's punctuation leaves the opening boundary of the al-Ghazali quotation unclear (only a closing quotation mark is present), so the quote was opened at the natural sentence boundary beginning 'This is the aim of the dhikr'.
comprehension_flags: The word 'initiatic' recurs in several places unglossed, and a first-time reader may stumble on it, but this pass is not authorized to add an explanation the source does not supply.
The term "apophasis" appears unglossed, and a general reader may not know it means the way of negation — describing God by denying attributes rather than affirming them.
terminology_notes: Shii — the adjective is standardized as 'Shii' throughout (the source's single 'Shiite 'Irfan' was regularized to match the spelling used everywhere else in the passage).

chapters.title: Remembrance as the Quintessence of Worship
Extinction and the Name: The Death of the Saint
comprehension_flags: The term haqiqa recurs as a keystone of the chapter ("the haqiqa of the dhikr") but is never plainly glossed, so a reader without Arabic must infer its sense of "inner reality/truth" from context.
A general reader may stumble on the unglossed specialist terms "exoteric mentality" and "gnosis," which the passage uses without explanation.
terminology_notes: haqiqa — recommend a consistent book-wide rendering or a single glossed first occurrence, since it carries the chapter's central claim about the dhikr.

chapters.title: The First Sermon of the Nahj al-Balagha
comprehension_flags: The negative-theology chain (every attribute affirmed only by being negated as the mind conceives it) is highly abstract and may lose a first-time reader, but no clarifying gloss beyond the source's own is authorized in this pass.
terminology_notes: servants (عباد) — the source alternates between "His slaves" and "God's servants" for the same term; standardized to "servants" throughout, matching the wording the later fiqh paragraph already uses.
